80BB3450DFE50131429F68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate buyers (e.g., a parent or caregiver) and sellers (e.g., a storeowner or other producer)

80BAA0F0DFE50131429D68A86D17958E.description: Explain people's basic needs and how they fulfill them

80BA1290DFE50131429B68A86D17958E.description: Resources, Markets, and Government — Understand economic concepts and the characteristics of various economic systems

80B96EC0DFE50131429968A86D17958E.description: Use terms to describe relative location (i.e., above/below, near/far, left/right, and cardinal directions)

80B92320DFE50131429868A86D17958E.description: Identify location and physical characteristics represented on maps and globes (e.g., land, water, roads, cities)

80B8A340DFE50131429668A86D17958E.description: World in Spatial Terms - Use geographic representations to organize, analyze, and present information on people, places, and environments and understand the nature and interaction of geographic regions and societies around the world

80B81A80DFE50131429468A86D17958E.description: Explain how and why people from different cultures observe different holidays/celebrations

80B75AB0DFE50131429268A86D17958E.description: Systems, Dynamics, and Inquiry — Understand culture as a system of beliefs, knowledge, and practices shared by a group and understand how cultural systems change over time

80B6DD30DFE50131429068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways to improve the quality of life in own school or community

80B65DE0DFE50131428E68A86D17958E.description: Describe his or her rights and demonstrate responsibilities of self in classroom, school, and neighborhood settings

80B5D050DFE50131428C68A86D17958E.description: Participation and Citizenship — Understand roles, rights (personal, economic, political), and responsibilities of American citizens and exercise them in civic action

80B59340DFE50131428B68A86D17958E.description: Identify rules that apply in different settings and the results from complying or not complying with these rules

80B51180DFE50131428968A86D17958E.description: Governance, Democracy, and Interaction — Understand the purpose and historical impact of political institutions, the principles and values of American constitutional democracy, and the similarities and differences in government across cultural perspectives

80B48C90DFE50131428768A86D17958E.description: Describe historically significant events and observances in American history

80B3F450DFE50131428568A86D17958E.description: Historical Content — Understand change, cause and effect, and continuity in history and contemporary life

80B3ADF0DFE50131428468A86D17958E.description: Historical Understanding: Inquiry, Empathy, and Perspective — Use the tools and methods of inquiry, perspective, and empathy to explain historical events with multiple interpretations and judge the past on its own terms

80B35960DFE50131428368A86D17958E.description: Explain change and continuity over time, using calendars and simple timelines

80B2C8C0DFE50131428168A86D17958E.description: Historical Understanding: Change, Continuity, and Causality — Understand change and/or continuity and cause and/or effect in history

7DBA9300DFE501313C9568A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7DBA2360DFE501313C9468A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., refined, respectful, polite, diplomatic, condescending).

7DB9BB00DFE501313C9368A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonym/antonym, analogy) to better understand each of the words.

7DB968A0DFE501313C9268A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., literary, biblical, and mythological allusions) in context.

7DB91010DFE501313C9168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7DB8BA70DFE501313C9068A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

7DB851C0DFE501313C8F68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

7DB7EB60DFE501313C8E68A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., belligerent, bellicose, rebel).

7DB78F40DFE501313C8D68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

7DB72CF0DFE501313C8C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

7DB683B0DFE501313C8A68A86D17958E.description: Choose language that expresses ideas precisely and concisely, recognizing and eliminating wordiness and redundancy.

7DB628F0DFE501313C8968A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

7DB52370DFE501313C8668A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate coordinate adjectives (e.g., It was a fascinating, enjoyable movie but not He wore an old[,] green shirt).

7DB4B360DFE501313C8568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7DB443F0DFE501313C8468A86D17958E.description: Place phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.

7DB3F470DFE501313C8368A86D17958E.description: Choose among simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

7DB3A490DFE501313C8268A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general and their function in specific sentences.

7DB35490DFE501313C8168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7DB253A0DFE501313C7E68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

7DB1B830DFE501313C7C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

7DB16720DFE501313C7B68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

7DB0B650DFE501313C7968A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

7DAFEF80DFE501313C7768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

7DAF93D0DFE501313C7668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

7DAEEA90DFE501313C7468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

7DAE8940DFE501313C7368A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

7DAE3B30DFE501313C7268A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify claims and findings and emphasize salient points.

7DADEE80DFE501313C7168A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with pertinent descriptions, facts, details, and examples; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

7DAD5480DFE501313C6F68A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

7DACFEC0DFE501313C6E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how the ideas clarify a topic, text, or issue under study.

7DAC9450DFE501313C6D68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others and, when warranted, modify their own views.

7DAC47E0DFE501313C6C68A86D17958E.description: Pose questions that elicit elaboration and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant observations and ideas that bring the discussion back on topic as needed.

7DABF880DFE501313C6B68A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

7DABA970DFE501313C6A68A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

7DAB4840DFE501313C6968A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 7 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

7DAA4FB0DFE501313C6668A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

7DA9FF50DFE501313C6568A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

7DA9AA70DFE501313C6468A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7DA35F90DFE501313C6268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

7DA30620DFE501313C6168A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

7DA2B490DFE501313C6068A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

7DA212A0DFE501313C5E68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

7DA1AB90DFE501313C5D68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7DA0C8F0DFE501313C5B68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7DA076E0DFE501313C5A68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

7DA01B70DFE501313C5968A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

7D9FCD20DFE501313C5868A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7D9F7EC0DFE501313C5768A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

7D9F31C0DFE501313C5668A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

7D9EE220DFE501313C5568A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7D9E2090DFE501313C5368A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

7D9DC550DFE501313C5268A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

7D9D7780DFE501313C5168A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

7D9D2830DFE501313C5068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

7D9CD720DFE501313C4F68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

7D9C81B0DFE501313C4E68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7D9C1F60DFE501313C4D68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

7D9BC930DFE501313C4C68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

7D9B7600DFE501313C4B68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7D9B2660DFE501313C4A68A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

7D9AD280DFE501313C4968A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

7D9A7B50DFE501313C4868A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

7D9A29F0DFE501313C4768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

7D996B20DFE501313C4568A86D17958E.description: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

7D990930DFE501313C4468A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7D9857C0DFE501313C4268A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g. "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims").

7D980C30DFE501313C4168A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 7 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history").

7D97C070DFE501313C4068A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7D977290DFE501313C3F68A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

7D972250DFE501313C3E68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions for further research and investigation.

7D96C630DFE501313C3D68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7D967410DFE501313C3C68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and link to and cite sources as well as to interact and collaborate with others, including linking to and citing sources.

7D960C40DFE501313C3B68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

7D9598A0DFE501313C3A68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7D94E960DFE501313C3868A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

7D949B20DFE501313C3768A86D17958E.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

7D944BB0DFE501313C3668A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence and signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another.

7D93F8B0DFE501313C3568A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, and description, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

7D9384E0DFE501313C3468A86D17958E.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

7D932390DFE501313C3368A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

7D92D0A0DFE501313C3268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented

7D927D90DFE501313C3168A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7D922710DFE501313C3068A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

7D91CA90DFE501313C2F68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

7D9167F0DFE501313C2E68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

7D9108A0DFE501313C2D68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

7D90B970DFE501313C2C68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content

7D906120DFE501313C2B68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

7D8FF380DFE501313C2A68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

7D8F9BD0DFE501313C2968A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.

7D8F4D40DFE501313C2868A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

7D8EFEC0DFE501313C2768A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

7D8EADB0DFE501313C2668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

7D8DB310DFE501313C2368A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

7D8D12F0DFE501313C2168A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

7D8CB8F0DFE501313C2068A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

7D8C52A0DFE501313C1F68A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

7D8BEF70DFE501313C1E68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

7D8BA020DFE501313C1D68A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

7D8B4F90DFE501313C1C68A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

7D8AF8C0DFE501313C1B68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

7D8A29F0DFE501313C1968A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

7D89DAC0DFE501313C1868A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

7D898AF0DFE501313C1768A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

7D88E4F0DFE501313C1568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

7D888F30DFE501313C1468A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend science/technical texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7D883E40DFE501313C1368A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7D87EEC0DFE501313C1268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the information gained from experiments, simulations, video, or multimedia sources with that gained from reading a text on the same topic.

7D879870DFE501313C1168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among facts, reasoned judgment based on research findings, and speculation in a text.

7D8739A0DFE501313C1068A86D17958E.description: Integrate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text with a version of that information expressed visually (e.g., in a flowchart, diagram, model, graph, or table).

7D867CB0DFE501313C0E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text.

7D862C50DFE501313C0D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to an understanding of the topic.

7D85D830DFE501313C0C68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 6—8 texts and topics.

7D851900DFE501313C0A68A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks.

7D84C450DFE501313C0968A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

7D847330DFE501313C0868A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

7D83C890DFE501313C0668A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

7D835980DFE501313C0568A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7D82F7A0DFE501313C0468A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7D82A0A0DFE501313C0368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

7D822A50DFE501313C0268A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

7D81BB40DFE501313C0168A86D17958E.description: Integrate visual information (e.g., in charts, graphs, photographs, videos, or maps) with other information in print and digital texts.

7D812430DFE501313BFF68A86D17958E.description: Identify aspects of a text that reveal an author's point of view or purpose (e.g., loaded language, inclusion or avoidance of particular facts).

7D80D6D0DFE501313BFE68A86D17958E.description: Describe how a text presents information (e.g., sequentially, comparatively, causally).

7D807D70DFE501313BFD68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

7D7FD140DFE501313BFB68A86D17958E.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

7D7F78A0DFE501313BFA68A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

7D7F27A0DFE501313BF968A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

7D7E7FB0DFE501313BF768A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

7D7E2790DFE501313BF668A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

7D7DCC50DFE501313BF568A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7D7D7B10DFE501313BF468A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more authors writing about the same topic shape their presentations of key information by emphasizing different evidence or advancing different interpretations of facts.

7D7D2500DFE501313BF368A86D17958E.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient to support the claims.

7D7CC330DFE501313BF268A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the text, analyzing each medium's portrayal of the subject (e.g., how the delivery of a speech affects the impact of the words).

7D7C1FF0DFE501313BF068A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.

7D7BCC70DFE501313BEF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas.

7D7B6350DFE501313BEE68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.

7D7AA760DFE501313BEC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in a text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events, or how individuals influence ideas or events).

7D7A4CC0DFE501313BEB68A86D17958E.description: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

7D79DDD0DFE501313BEA68A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

7D78C160DFE501313BE768A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6–8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

7D787240DFE501313BE668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7D77BDA0DFE501313BE468A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a fictional portrayal of a time, place, or character and a historical account of the same period as a means of understanding how authors of fiction use or alter history.

7D776890DFE501313BE368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a written story, drama, or poem to its audio, filmed, staged, or multimedia version, analyzing the effects of techniques unique to each medium (e.g., lighting, sound, color, or camera focus and angles in a film).

7D76C110DFE501313BE168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author develops and contrasts the points of view of different characters or narrators in a text.

7D7668C0DFE501313BE068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a drama's or poem's form or structure (e.g., soliloquy, sonnet) contributes to its meaning.

7D761350DFE501313BDF68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama.

7D754F90DFE501313BDD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

7D74EFE0DFE501313BDC68A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

7D7499E0DFE501313BDB68A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

7D736B80DFE501313BD868A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

7D731E20DFE501313BD768A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7D72D130DFE501313BD668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

7D728260DFE501313BD568A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

7D721D60DFE501313BD468A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

7D718280DFE501313BD268A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

7D7132D0DFE501313BD168A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

7D70DF40DFE501313BD068A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

7D701220DFE501313BCE68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

7D6FBEC0DFE501313BCD68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

7D6F64D0DFE501313BCC68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

7D6EA5B0DFE501313BCA68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Hawaii Content and Performance Standards for Social Studies

81CBAA20DFE50131442768A86D17958E.description: Describe the factors that influence production and consumption decisions in a market system

81CAF1B0DFE50131442568A86D17958E.description: Explain productivity in terms of output per worker, hour, machine, or unit of land, and its effects on standards of living in 18th and/or 19th century America

81CA6B60DFE50131442368A86D17958E.description: Resources, Markets, and Government — Understand economic concepts and the characteristics of various economic systems

81C9E310DFE50131442168A86D17958E.description: World in Spatial Terms - Use geographic representations to organize, analyze, and present information on people, places, and environments and understand the nature and interaction of geographic regions and societies around the world

81C96100DFE50131441F68A86D17958E.description: Systems, Dynamics, and Inquiry — Understand culture as a system of beliefs, knowledge, and practices shared by a group and understand how cultural systems change over time

81C8B500DFE50131441D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the responsibilities of citizens in a representative democracy

81C828A0DFE50131441B68A86D17958E.description: Participation and Citizenship — Understand roles, rights (personal, economic, political), and responsibilities of American citizens and exercise them in civic action

81C7E990DFE50131441A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the influences of America on other nations and/or organizations and vice versa (including French and Spanish interests at the start of the Lewis and Clark Expedition and the impact of the Indian removals)

81C7AB10DFE50131441968A86D17958E.description: Explain United States foreign policy as reflected in the Monroe Doctrine

81C72B10DFE50131441768A86D17958E.description: Describe the purpose and structures of the three branches of the federal government

81C683A0DFE50131441568A86D17958E.description: Governance, Democracy, and Interaction — Understand the purpose and historical impact of political institutions, the principles and values of American constitutional democracy, and the similarities and differences in government across cultural perspectives

81C5E230DFE50131441368A86D17958E.description: Explain the impact of the Civil War on African Americans

81C5A4F0DFE50131441268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the Reconstruction plan of President Lincoln and that of the congressional Republicans

81C52720DFE50131441068A86D17958E.description: Explain the major factors that determined the outcome of the Civil War (including leaders, resources, and key battles)

81C4DF70DFE50131440F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the key issues and events after the Mexican War relate to the outbreak of the Civil War

81C46580DFE50131440D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the sectionalism that emerged in the first half of the 19th century

81C3E640DFE50131440B68A86D17958E.description: Examine how and why the United States became a continental nation through westward expansion

81C34090DFE50131440968A86D17958E.description: Describe significant events and changes associated with Andrew Jackson's presidency (including Jackson's stance on Indian removal issues and Jacksonian democracy)

81C2D870DFE50131440868A86D17958E.description: Describe the emergence of the two party system (including Washington's farewell address and the election of 1800)

81C29B90DFE50131440768A86D17958E.description: Early Government of the United States

81C25D10DFE50131440668A86D17958E.description: Describe how the development of technology in the first half of the 19th century had an impact on American life

81C21C60DFE50131440568A86D17958E.description: Examine the impact of the Seneca Falls Convention and major abolitionists, including Frederick Douglass and William Lloyd Garrison

81C1CD10DFE50131440468A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Bill of Rights places limitations on the federal government

81C14020DFE50131440268A86D17958E.description: Explain the controversies over the ratification of the Constitution

81C0F650DFE50131440168A86D17958E.description: Describe the ideas and principles (including checks and balances, separation of powers, representative democracy) of the Constitution

81C0B8B0DFE50131440068A86D17958E.description: Describe the controversies (including large states versus small states and slavery) and the compromises that resolved them (including the Great Compromise and the Three-Fifths Compromise) at the Constitutional Convention

81C07B00DFE5013143FF68A86D17958E.description: Explain the problems of the national government under the Articles of Confederation that led to the Constitutional Convention of 1787

81BFFD10DFE5013143FD68A86D17958E.description: United States History — Understand important historical events in the Post-Revolutionary war through Reconstruction era (including Second Great Awakening and westward expansion)

81BFBBA0DFE5013143FC68A86D17958E.description: Describe why different people may have different perspectives of the same historical event and multiple interpretations should be considered in order to avoid historical linearity and inevitability

81BF26C0DFE5013143FA68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between primary and secondary sources, understanding the potential and limitations of each

81BE9470DFE5013143F868A86D17958E.description: Historical Understanding: Inquiry, Empathy, and Perspective — Use the tools and methods of inquiry, perspective, and empathy to explain historical events with multiple interpretations and judge the past on its own terms

81BE2D30DFE5013143F768A86D17958E.description: Historical Understanding: Change, Continuity, and Causality — Understand change and/or continuity and cause and/or effect in history

8358E3E0DFE50131471A68A86D17958E.description: Perform a folk/traditional dance from another culture

83589FA0DFE50131471968A86D17958E.description: How the Arts Shape and Reflect Culture

835863D0DFE50131471868A86D17958E.description: Use movement to respond to a variety of stimuli, such as observed dance, words, sounds and songs

83582630DFE50131471768A86D17958E.description: Create movements that represent ideas, persons, and places

83578D00DFE50131471568A86D17958E.description: Use body, energy, space, and time to move in different ways

835702A0DFE50131471368A86D17958E.description: Dance — Understand and apply elements of dance, appreciate how dance communicates meaning, and recognize its role across cultures and throughout history

8356C4D0DFE50131471268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how cultures have used dramatic play to express human experience

83568440DFE50131471168A86D17958E.description: How the Arts Shape and Reflect Culture

83563D20DFE50131471068A86D17958E.description: Explain how theatrical performances often cause emotional reactions

83550890DFE50131470C68A86D17958E.description: Drama and Theatre — Understand and apply the skills of acting, design, and technical theatre and understand the role of drama in various cultures throughout history

8354C610DFE50131470B68A86D17958E.description: Identify various sources of music that can be heard in daily life and their purpose

83548160DFE50131470A68A86D17958E.description: How the Arts Shape and Reflect Culture

83543E70DFE50131470968A86D17958E.description: Use an instrument to maintain a steady beat using quarter notes and quarter rests

8353BF80DFE50131470768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate simple representation of high and low, short and long, loud and soft, fast and slow

83538430DFE50131470668A86D17958E.description: Use singing voice to echo short melodic patterns in appropriate range

83530670DFE50131470468A86D17958E.description: Music — Understand and apply elements of music and understand how music communicates ideas, feelings, and experiences across cultures

8352BA40DFE50131470368A86D17958E.description: Explain the concept that all artwork is meant to be appreciated and some artwork is also meant to be useful

83527270DFE50131470268A86D17958E.description: How the Arts Shape and Reflect Culture

835225F0DFE50131470168A86D17958E.description: Explain preferences for particular works of art

8351EB10DFE50131470068A86D17958E.description: Create art that expresses feelings about a familiar subject

83517270DFE5013146FE68A86D17958E.description: Use developmentally appropriate art media, tools, and processes

8350A310DFE5013146FB68A86D17958E.description: Visual Arts — Understand and apply art materials, techniques, and processes in the creation of original works of art and understand how the visual arts communicate a variety of ideas, feelings, and experiences

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

7745D390DFE50131311168A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

773F8910DFE50131311068A86D17958E.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.
comments: Example: express 3 in the form 3 = 3/1; recognize that 6/1 = 6.
Example: locate 4/4 and 1 at the same point of a number line diagram.

773F3BD0DFE50131310F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3). Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

773EF7E0DFE50131310E68A86D17958E.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

773EAA30DFE50131310D68A86D17958E.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

773E6340DFE50131310C68A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.

773E1FA0DFE50131310B68A86D17958E.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

773DD360DFE50131310A68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

773D8190DFE50131310968A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

773D3BD0DFE50131310868A86D17958E.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

773CB1F0DFE50131310668A86D17958E.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
comments: For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as 1/4 of the area of the shape.

773C6960DFE50131310568A86D17958E.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombuses, rectangles, and others) may share attributes (e.g., having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

773C1F70DFE50131310468A86D17958E.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

773B8C20DFE50131310268A86D17958E.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

773B3D50DFE50131310168A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

773AEF30DFE50131310068A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

773A9C70DFE5013130FF68A86D17958E.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

773A55F0DFE5013130FE68A86D17958E.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

773A0100DFE5013130FD68A86D17958E.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

7739B9C0DFE5013130FC68A86D17958E.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

77396FA0DFE5013130FB68A86D17958E.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

77391A10DFE5013130FA68A86D17958E.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units.

7738CED0DFE5013130F968A86D17958E.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area.

773881C0DFE5013130F868A86D17958E.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

773834C0DFE5013130F768A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

77372A30DFE5013130F368A86D17958E.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

comments: For example, draw a bar graph in which each square in the bar graph might represent 5 pets.
7736DDB0DFE5013130F268A86D17958E.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

7737F0B0DFE5013130F668A86D17958E.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, e.g., by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.
comments: Excludes multiplicative comparison problems (problems involving notions of "times as much";
Excludes compound units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container.

7737AF60DFE5013130F568A86D17958E.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, e.g., by representing the problem on a number line diagram.

77376F80DFE5013130F468A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

7735EE10DFE5013130EF68A86D17958E.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10—90 (e.g., 9 × 80, 5 × 60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

7735A0C0DFE5013130EE68A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

77355DF0DFE5013130ED68A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

77351410DFE5013130EC68A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.
comments: A range of algorithms may be used.

7734C570DFE5013130EB68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.
For example, observe that 4 times a number is always even, and explain why 4 times a number can be decomposed into two equal addends.
77348350DFE5013130EA68A86D17958E.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

77343F70DFE5013130E968A86D17958E.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.
comments: This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers; students should know how to perform operations in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

7733FC50DFE5013130E868A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

7733A540DFE5013130E768A86D17958E.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations. By the end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

7732F5F0DFE5013130E568A86D17958E.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
comments: For example, find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.

7732B1D0DFE5013130E468A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
comments: Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
Example: Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.)

Example: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known (Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.)

77326FA0DFE5013130E368A86D17958E.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

773229D0DFE5013130E268A86D17958E.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
comments: For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 × ? = 48, 5 = ÷ 3, 6 × 6 = ?.

7731E480DFE5013130E168A86D17958E.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

comments: For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as 56 ÷ 8.
77318EA0DFE5013130E068A86D17958E.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

77313EB0DFE5013130DF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.
comments: For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as 5 × 7.

7730FCB0DFE5013130DE68A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
77306C70DFE5013130DC68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
77301F70DFE5013130DB68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.
772EDEC0DFE5013130D768A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

comments: Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

772E2D40DFE5013130D568A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
8BAA620AED37490B82D24FEB6DFFCEEB.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.
9367A3485D414D5A8C597F74B256023F.description: Look for and make use of structure.

comments: Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

430F41868AF3440B8784C248AE5AD53A.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

7E73A710DFE501313DAF68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7E735CC0DFE501313DAE68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast findings presented in a text to those from other sources (including their own experiments), noting when the findings support or contradict previous explanations or accounts.

7E7311B0DFE501313DAD68A86D17958E.description: Assess the extent to which the reasoning and evidence in a text support the author's claim or a recommendation for solving a scientific or technical problem.

7E72C5A0DFE501313DAC68A86D17958E.description: Translate quantitative or technical information expressed in words in a text into visual form (e.g., a table or chart) and translate information expressed visually or mathematically (e.g., in an equation) into words.

7E722270DFE501313DAA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the author's purpose in providing an explanation, describing a procedure, or discussing an experiment in a text, defining the question the author seeks to address.

7E71CF00DFE501313DA968A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of the relationships among concepts in a text, including relationships among key terms (e.g., force, friction, reaction force, energy).

7E717D30DFE501313DA868A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of symbols, key terms, and other domain-specific words and phrases as they are used in a specific scientific or technical context relevant to grades 9—10 texts and topics.

7E70E700DFE501313DA668A86D17958E.description: Follow precisely a complex multistep procedure when carrying out experiments, taking measurements, or performing technical tasks, attending to special cases or exceptions defined in the text.

7E7091C0DFE501313DA568A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; trace the text's explanation or depiction of a complex process, phenomenon, or concept; provide an accurate summary of the text.

7E7042A0DFE501313DA468A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts, attending to the precise details of explanations or descriptions.

7E6FA350DFE501313DA268A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in Science and Technical Subjects 6—12

7E6F5070DFE501313DA168A86D17958E.description: By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7E6EFCE0DFE501313DA068A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7E6EA810DFE501313D9F68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast treatments of the same topic in several primary and secondary sources.

7E6E59A0DFE501313D9E68A86D17958E.description: Assess the extent to which the reasoning and evidence in a text support the author's claims.

7E6E0A30DFE501313D9D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate quantitative or technical analysis (e.g., charts, research data) with qualitative analysis in print or digital text.

7E6D6750DFE501313D9B68A86D17958E.description: Compare the point of view of two or more authors for how they treat the same or similar topics, including which details they include and emphasize in their respective accounts.

7E6D0960DFE501313D9A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how a text uses structure to emphasize key points or advance an explanation or analysis

7E6CAC60DFE501313D9968A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary describing political, social, or economic aspects of history/social studies.

7E6BE3D0DFE501313D9768A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail a series of events described in a text; determine whether earlier events caused later ones or simply preceded them.

7E6B8CB0DFE501313D9668A86D17958E.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of how key events or ideas develop over the course of the text.

7E6B37D0DFE501313D9568A86D17958E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, attending to such features as the date and origin of the information.

7E6A54B0DFE501313D9268A86D17958E.description:

By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7E6A04F0DFE501313D9168A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7E69AF90DFE501313D9068A86D17958E.description: Analyze seminal U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (e.g., Washington's Farewell Address, the Gettysburg Address, Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech, King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail"), including how they address related themes and concepts.

7E696010DFE501313D8F68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

7E690FF0DFE501313D8E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums (e.g., a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

7E686A70DFE501313D8C68A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

7E680FB0DFE501313D8B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text (e.g., a section or chapter).

7E662860DFE501313D8668A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

7E652210DFE501313D8368A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 9—10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

7E64D350DFE501313D8268A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7E642750DFE501313D8068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

7E63D480DFE501313D7F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).
